boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Cold Harbor record (May 31-June 12, 1864) in Grant's Overland Campaign [May-June 1864]. Trevilian Station (VA099, June 11–12) is a separate cavalry record; the James crossing after June 12 is outside the interval. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. Imported numerical estimates remain unchanged; this pass does not validate them as simultaneous opening forces.

claims.value: The frozen and live force fields read 170,000 (US 108,000; CS 62,000). Humphreys says Smith landed about 12,500 men, left 2,500 with Ames and marched with 10,000 and sixteen guns; that Hoke's division joined Lee with a little less than 6,000 enlisted infantry; and that Wilson was reinforced by a nominal 3,000 infantry and 2,000 cavalry, of which Wilson reported about 1,400 efficient infantry and 1,000 good cavalry.
claims.rationale: Partial figures for arriving forces, not matched opening strengths. None is adopted as a matched opening strength; live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. NPS says the June 3 assaults were slaughtered at all points; Meade says the Sixth and Eighteenth Corps assaults failed and offensive operations closed about 11 a.m.; Humphreys dates the suspension order to half-past one and says the army remained until the night of June 12.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Meade's and Humphreys' times for the end of the offensive differ.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 15,500 (US 13,000; CS 2,500); the live field reads 18,000 (US 13,000; CS 5,000). Humphreys says the three assaulting corps lost over 4,000 killed and wounded in about an hour on June 3, and over 5,600 including the Fifth and Ninth Corps; for June 1 and 3 he gives 8,411 killed and wounded and 9,948 in all, and the medical director's grand total of 14,129 from the Pamunkey to June 12 including the Eighteenth Corps. For Lee's army he gives the Medical and Surgical History's 1,200 wounded and 500 missing for June 1–12, says the actual number was probably much greater, and estimates four to five thousand for May 27–June 12.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Humphreys' periods (June 3, June 1 and 3, May 27–June 12) overlap and are not additive.

open_questions: Smith's, Wright's, Hancock's, Warren's and Burnside's reports, Lee's dispatches, the Longstreet corps diary, Sheridan's May 31–June 1 dispatches (read; garbled; not selected) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan, and it shares headquarters papers with Meade's and Sheridan's reports. Meade's, Sheridan's, Hampton's, Butler's and Wild's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXXVI, Parts 1 and 2, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
